newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major accuses Labour of inconsistency.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major accuses Labour of inconsistency.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Thursday accused the opposition Labour Party of constantly changing its policy line, saying "one day they are fighting cocks, the next day they are chickens".
"It must be very confusing to the electorate," Major told a news conference.
Major said the voters could not trust Labour when its leader Tony Blair made contradictory statements, for instance on how he would deal with Britain's relations with Europe.

"How can you trust Labour when Mr Blair claims here that he'll stand up for British interests in Europe after he tells his European socialist colleagues abroad that he'll never let Britain be isolated," Major said.
Speaking an hour ahead of the launch of Labour's election manifesto, Major predicted it would be "phoney".
Labour is widely tipped to win the May 1 election, with the ruling Conservatives trailing badly in opinion polls.
"I predict they will tell you all of what they won't do but only some of what they will do. But what's left out is more important that what's left in," Major said.

Major predicted that within six weeks of taking power a Labour government would sell out British interests in Europe, within three months it would raise taxes by billions of pounds (dollars) and that within a year, it would hand more power back to trade unions.
